theme.title: Shortened seasons
theme.subtitle: Lockouts and the pandemic
theme.recap: The NBA has cut its schedule to 50 games, 66 games and 72 games, and the shortened years still produced champions.

questions.prompt: The 1998–99 lockout cut the regular season to how many games per team?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Due to a lockout, the regular season began on February 5, 1999, and was cut from 82 games to 50.

funFacts.text: The season began unusually late after the league and players' association settled their labor dispute.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the season, which began on February 5, 1999

funFacts.text: Chicago's championship dynasty disintegrated during the stoppage, with Jordan and Phil Jackson leaving.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Phil Jackson and Michael Jordan temporarily retire

funFacts.text: The New York Knicks reached the Finals from the bottom playoff seed, an extraordinary outcome.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: this was the only NBA Finals to feature an eighth-seeded team

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)

funFacts.text: The pandemic pushed the Bucks–Suns championship series into July, far later than the normal schedule.

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 1998–99 Spurs win in the lockout season?
questions.note: 37, going 37–13, tied with Utah for the league’s best.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Spurs finished in first place in the Midwest Division with a league-best 37–13 record

funFacts.text: The Spurs started slowly before tearing through March and the rest of the shortened schedule.

source.quote: the Spurs got off to a slow start to the regular season by posting a 6–8 record in February
